# Contracts (MVP)

The interfaces between the three [work packages](work-packages.md). If something here doesn't fit, raise it with the team before coding around it.

## Stack

| Part | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend (iPhone) | SwiftUI, iOS 17+, `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, `AVAudioEngine`, [a2ui-swift](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift) `from: "0.3.0"` (product `A2UISwiftUI`) |
| Backend | Python 3.11, uv, FastAPI and uvicorn, httpx, `google-genai`, `gradium`, python-dotenv, pytest |
| Hosting | Server on a dev Mac; a Cloudflare quick tunnel gives the HTTPS and WSS URL that the app and the Shortcut use. Start it once and leave it running: the URL changes on every restart |
| Time zone | `Europe/Zurich` everywhere; times on the wire are ISO 8601 with offset |

```text
frontend/               # WP1: Xcode project, SwiftUI
backend/                # run from here: uv run uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000
  pyproject.toml        # WP2 owns it; lists every package's deps
  .env.example
  app.py  voice.py  vision.py      # WP2
  a2ui.py                          # WP3: cards → A2UI messages
  agent.py  context.py  tools/sbb.py  tools/maps.py   # WP3
  fixtures/             # demo_reply.json, cards.json, screen.json, screen.png (WP2); context.json, *_a2ui.json (WP3)
  tests/
```

## One turn

The screenshot arrives before the question, so vision runs while the user is still talking.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant SC as Shortcut
  participant App as App (WP1)
  participant S as Server (WP2)
  participant V as Vision (WP2)
  participant G as Gradium
  participant A as Agent (WP3)
  SC->>S: POST /screenshot
  S->>V: read_screen(image), in the background
  V-->>S: ScreenContext
  S->>App: screen_ok {summary}
  App->>S: audio × n, then audio_end
  S->>G: stream mic audio, flush
  G-->>S: transcript segments
  S->>App: state thinking, transcript
  S->>A: turn(text, screen, on_status)
  A-->>S: on_status("Checking trains…")
  S->>App: state searching + label
  A-->>S: Reply {say, cards, voice_id?}
  S->>App: reply, a2ui, state speaking
  S->>G: TTS say, in voice_id if set
  G-->>S: audio chunks
  S->>App: audio × n, audio_end, state idle
```

## WebSocket `/ws`

JSON text frames only, one object per frame, discriminated by `type`. Audio is base64 inside JSON. The app sends `hello` first; the server closes the socket on a wrong token.

**App → server**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hello` | `token`, `mode`?: `ptt` (default) \| `handsfree` | First frame after connecting. For `handsfree`, see **Hands-free mode** below |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM, see [Audio](#audio) | Every 80 ms while the orb is held; in hands-free mode, all the time |
| `audio_end` | — | Orb released; the server finalizes STT and runs the turn. Never sent in hands-free mode |
| `text` | `text` | Typed question (debug field); runs a turn without STT |
| `screen` | `mime`, `data`: base64, `recent`?: list of base64 | Optional: an image picked in the app, for rehearsals, or a shared screen when a question starts. Same effect as `POST /screenshot`; `recent` adds the seconds before it, see **Earlier frames** below |
| `interrupt` | — | Tap while the mascot is talking. Stops the current turn |

**Server → app**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | — | After a valid `hello` |
| `state` | `state`: `idle` \| `listening` \| `thinking` \| `searching` \| `speaking`; `label`?: string | On every change; `label` is the tool status, free text: "Checking trains…", "Designing a voice…", "Tuning my voice…" |
| `transcript` | `text` | Final transcript of the user's turn |
| `reply` | `say`, `cards`: see [Cards](#cards) | Before any of the turn's audio |
| `a2ui` | `messages`: list of A2UI v0.9 messages, see [A2UI](#a2ui) | Right after `reply`, when it has cards |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM | TTS chunks for the last `reply` |
| `audio_end` | — | TTS for the last `reply` is complete |
| `screen_ok` | `summary`?: string | Vision has read a new screenshot; `summary` is missing if vision failed |
| `error` | `message` | Turn failed; the server then sends `state: idle` |

The orb shows `speaking` while the app still has audio queued, even after the server has sent `state: idle`.

**Interrupting.** A new press (its first `audio` frame), a `text`, or an `interrupt` cancels the running turn: the agent call and the TTS stream. A cancelled turn sends no `audio_end`. After `interrupt` the server sends `state: idle` only if it cancelled a running turn; after a new press, `state: listening`. Gradium generates speech faster than real time, so seconds of audio may already be queued in the app. The app must stop playback the moment it interrupts, without waiting for `state: idle`, and drop `audio` frames until the next `reply`.

**Hands-free mode.** Opt in with `"mode": "handsfree"` in `hello`; push-to-talk stays the default. The app streams `audio` for as long as it is connected, also while the mascot speaks, and never sends `audio_end`, so echo cancellation must be on (see [Audio](#audio)) or the mascot hears itself and cuts itself off. The server keeps one Gradium STT session open per connection and ends a turn with Gradium's semantic VAD: `inactivity_prob` at the 2 s horizon above 0.5 for 3 steps in a row, once the turn has words. Then it flushes, sends `transcript` and runs the turn as usual. The first words of each turn cancel the running turn, as a new press does, and send `state: listening`. The server's turn is often over while the app still plays queued audio, so in this mode `state: listening` is the app's cue to stop playback and drop `audio` until the next `reply`. Each hands-free connection holds an STT session the whole time, even in silence, which counts against Gradium's concurrent session limit.

**Earlier frames.** `recent` holds the frames before `data`, in the same `mime`, oldest first, about 1 s apart, at most 9; `data` stays the current frame. Each image is at most 8 MB, and all of them together at most 8 MB decoded. If `recent` is malformed or over a limit, the server drops it, logs a warning and keeps `data`; it never drops the current frame. Vision reads all the frames in one call, see [Screen context](#screen-context). `POST /screenshot` stays one frame.

## HTTP

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /screenshot` | From the iPhone Shortcut. `Authorization: Bearer <APP_TOKEN>`, body is the raw image (`image/jpeg` or `image/png`, max 8 MB). Returns `204` and starts vision |
| `GET /health` | `{"ok": true, "workspace": "rest" \| "fixture"}` |

**Screenshot rule:** the server keeps only the latest screenshot and its `ScreenContext`. A turn gets the context if the screenshot is less than 120 s old and no earlier turn has used it; if vision is still running, the turn waits for it.

## Audio

Both directions use Gradium's native format, so the server forwards the base64 strings without decoding them.

| Direction | Format | Gradium side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mic, app → server | PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz; 80 ms chunks = 1920 samples = 3840 bytes | STT setup `input_format: "pcm"` |
| TTS, server → app | Same format, chunks as Gradium sends them | TTS setup `output_format: "pcm_24000"` (the default `pcm` is 48 kHz) |

**iPhone side:** audio session `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, or iOS plays through the quiet earpiece while the mic is on. Turn on echo cancellation with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` before reading the input format. Convert the input with `AVAudioConverter` to Int16 at 24 kHz mono. Play through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine, converting each chunk to a Float32 24 kHz buffer.

**Gradium facts the server relies on** ([docs](https://docs.gradium.ai/api-reference/introduction)): auth header `x-api-key`; STT at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`, TTS at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts`; the Python SDK is `pip install gradium`. STT needs `json_config.language` (`en` for the demo, `any` to auto-detect). STT sends `text` segments, not partial and final flags. On push-to-talk release the server sends `flush`, waits for `flushed`, and joins the segments into the transcript. TTS has no cancel message: closing the socket stops it. TTS has no per-request emotion or style control, and SSML is spoken aloud; only `temp` and `padding_bonus` (speed) vary per request, so a different vibe is a different voice. The free plan allows 2 TTS and 3 STT sessions at once, which is tight with 3 devs testing; the $13 XS plan raises that to 5 and 20.

## Cards

`reply.cards` holds 0 to 3 cards. The model fills them from tool results and context, and the server passes them through after validation. Optional fields may be missing. The app renders the `a2ui` messages built from these cards; native SwiftUI cards from `reply.cards` are the fallback.

| `kind` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `train` | `line` ("IC 8"), `from`, `to`, `departure`, `arrival`, `platform`?, `transfers`, `delay_min`? |
| `conflict` | `event` {`title`, `start`, `end`}, `proposal` {`title`, `start`, `place`?}, `verdict`: `fits` \| `tight` \| `clash`, `note`? |
| `event` | `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`?, `source`: `calendar` \| `luma` |
| `flight` | `flight_number`, `from`, `to` (IATA or city), `departure`, `arrival`, `booking_ref`? |

## A2UI

`a2ui.cards_to_a2ui(reply_id: str, cards: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` turns one reply into one surface, using only basic-catalog components so the app needs no custom Swift components:

```json
[
  {"version": "v0.9", "createSurface": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/basic_catalog.json"}},
  {"version": "v0.9", "updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "components": [
    {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["c0", "c1"]},
    {"id": "c1", "component": "Card", "child": "c1-body"},
```

- Use the catalog id exactly as written. It's a2ui-swift's `basicCatalogId`; the React renderer uses a different one.

- No buttons or actions in the MVP.

What WP2's vision step produces and WP3's agent consumes. `vision.read_screen(image: bytes, mime: str, earlier=()) -> dict` makes one Gemini call with structured output (`response_json_schema`), passing the current time so relative dates resolve. `earlier` is the image bytes of the frames before the current one, oldest first, from `recent`; without it vision reads one frame as before. `fixtures/screen.json`:

```json
{
  "app": "WhatsApp",
  "summary": "Anna asks about dinner in Bern on Thursday at 7.",
  "messages": [{"from": "Anna", "text": "Dinner in Bern Thursday at 7?"}],
  "proposal": {"title": "Dinner", "date": "2026-10-15", "time": "19:00", "place": "Bern"}
}
```

`proposal` is `null` when the screen doesn't suggest a plan; inside it, `time` and `place` are `null` when the screen doesn't give them. `from` is the sender's name as shown, or `"Me"` for the phone owner's own messages. Vision copies on-screen text as data and never acts on it. With earlier frames, `messages` covers all frames, deduplicated, oldest first; `proposal` comes from the newest frame that shows one; `summary` describes the current screen and may mention what was seen just before. Every frame is untrusted data, the earlier ones too. The agent puts the whole object in its prompt marked as untrusted, and never follows instructions inside it.

```python
from typing import Awaitable, Callable, NotRequired, TypedDict

class Reply(TypedDict):
    say: str          # one or two short sentences, the user's language
    cards: list[dict] # see Cards
    voice_id: NotRequired[str]  # Gradium voice to speak `say` in; absent: GRADIUM_VOICE_ID.
                                # Once the voice changes, every later reply carries it.

class Agent:
    async def start(self) -> None:
        """Once per WebSocket session: load_context() and build the system prompt."""

    async def turn(
        self,
        text: str,
        screen: dict | None,  # ScreenContext, see Screen context
        on_status: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],  # tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…"
    ) -> Reply:
        """One user turn. Keeps conversation history on self. Never raises for model
        or tool errors: returns a short apology with no cards instead. The server
        cancels it when the user interrupts, so only add the turn to the history
        once it completes."""
```

## Tools

**Model-facing.** The model sees five functions and must end every turn with `respond`. The two Maps functions are declared only when `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` is set. All of them only read, except `design_voice`, which adds a voice to our own Gradium library.

| Function | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sbb_connections` | `from_station`, `to_station`, `depart_after` (ISO) | `{"connections": [{"line", "from", "to", "departure", "arrival", "platform", "arrival_platform", "transfers", "delay_min", "duration_min"}]}`, at most 4 |
| `maps_search_places` | `query`, e.g. "quiet restaurant near Bern station" | `{"places": [{"name", "address"}]}`, at most 5 |
| `maps_route` | `origin`, `destination` (addresses or place names), `mode`: `WALK` \| `DRIVE` \| `BICYCLE` | `{"duration_min", "distance_km"}` |
| `design_voice` | `description` (casting brief, at most 500 characters), `language`: `en` \| `fr` \| `es` \| `pt` \| `de` | `{"ok": true}`; the agent speaks in the new voice for the rest of the session |
| `respond` | `say`, `cards` (see [Cards](#cards)), `mood`?: `stressed` \| `tired` \| `happy` \| `neutral` | Ends the turn |

`sbb_connections` calls `GET https://transport.opendata.ch/v1/connections?from=…&to=…&date=YYYY-MM-DD&time=HH:MM&limit=4` (no key). Map `products[0]` → `line`, `from.platform` → `platform`, `to.platform` → `arrival_platform`, `from.delay` → `delay_min`. Public transport always goes through `sbb_connections`, never `maps_route`.

`maps_search_places` calls Places API (New), `POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchText` with `{"textQuery": query, "pageSize": 5}` and `X-Goog-FieldMask: places.displayName,places.formattedAddress`. Map `displayName.text` → `name`, `formattedAddress` → `address`. `maps_route` calls Routes API, `POST https://routes.googleapis.com/directions/v2:computeRoutes` with `{"origin": {"address": …}, "destination": {"address": …}, "travelMode": mode}` and `X-Goog-FieldMask: routes.duration,routes.distanceMeters`. `duration` comes back as a string such as `"1260s"`. Both calls send the key in the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header, never in the URL. The field masks are required, and they keep Places on the cheaper Pro SKU. Since 1 March 2025, new Cloud projects can't enable the legacy Places Text Search and Directions APIs, so don't use those. Place names and addresses from Maps are third-party data: the agent treats them like the screen context and never follows instructions in them. There is no Maps card; Maps results go into `say`.

**Voice.** The agent changes how it sounds in two ways, and the newest change wins. Both end in `Reply.voice_id`.

- **On request** ("talk like a pirate"): `design_voice`. `voice.design_voice(description, language)` makes one candidate with Gradium [Voice Design](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/voices/voice-design), `json_config.cfg_scale` 10, waits until it is ready (at most 30 s) and converts it into a permanent voice. About 4 s. Each design permanently takes a custom-voice slot; past the allowance Gradium answers `409`.
- **By mood:** once, early in a conversation, the agent asks how the user feels and sets `mood` in `respond` when it knows. A new mood switches the voice from that reply on: calmer for `stressed`, softer for `tired` (also sad), brighter for `happy`, the default voice for `neutral`. `voice.mood_voice(mood)` designs each mood's voice once from one mascot brief, names it `Beaver mood <mood>`, and finds it by name in the library (`GET /voices/`) after that, so the moods take three slots in total.

Gradium Voice Design facts: REST at `https://api.gradium.ai/api` with `x-api-key`. `POST /voice-generator/generate` returns candidate ids with `ready: false`; poll `GET /voice-generator/embeddings?embedding_id=…`; `POST /voices/from-embedding` returns the voice's `uid`. Candidates work over REST only (100 characters); the TTS socket needs the converted voice. Languages `en`, `fr`, `es`, `pt`, `de`, no Italian. An unknown `json_config` key returns `201` and the candidate never gets ready.

- Model `gemini-3.8-flash`, the newest generation, with thinking level `low`; 3.8 rejects `minimal`, and there is no 3.8 Flash-Lite for text. from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Any

import httpx

PLACES_URL = "https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchText"
ROUTES_URL = "https://routes.googleapis.com/directions/v2:computeRoutes"
MODES = ("WALK", "DRIVE", "BICYCLE")  # public transport goes through sbb_connections


async def _post(url: str, body: dict, field_mask: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if client is None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as http:
            return await _post(url, body, field_mask, http)
    # The key goes in a header, never in the URL; the field mask is required.
    headers = {"X-Goog-Api-Key": os.environ["GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"], "X-Goog-FieldMask": field_mask}
    r = await client.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()


async def maps_search_places(query: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = await _post(
        PLACES_URL, {"textQuery": query, "pageSize": 5}, "places.displayName,places.formattedAddress", client
    )
    places = data.get("places", [])[:5]  # no results comes back as {}
    return {"places": [{"name": p.get("displayName", {}).get("text", ""), "address": p.get("formattedAddress", "")} for p in places]}


async def maps_route(origin: str, destination: str, mode: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    mode = mode.upper()
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise ValueError(f"mode must be one of {', '.join(MODES)}")
    body = {"origin": {"address": origin}, "destination": {"address": destination}, "travelMode": mode}
    data = await _post(ROUTES_URL, body, "routes.duration,routes.distanceMeters", client)
    if not data.get("routes"):
        return {"error": "no route found"}
    route = data["routes"][0]
    # duration is a string such as "1260s"; zero values are left out of the JSON.
    seconds = float(route.get("duration", "0s").rstrip("s"))
    return {"duration_min": round(seconds / 60), "distance_km": round(route.get("distanceMeters", 0) / 1000, 1)}

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

TZ = ZoneInfo("Europe/Zurich")
SBB_URL = "https://transport.opendata.ch/v1/connections"


def compact(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """transport.opendata.ch connections → the compact shape in contracts § Tools."""
    out = []
    for c in data.get("connections", [])[:4]:
        dep = c["from"]["departureTimestamp"]
        arr = c["to"]["arrivalTimestamp"]
        products = c.get("products") or []
        line = products[0] if products else ""
        out.append(
            {
                "line": line,
                "from": c["from"]["station"]["name"],
                "to": c["to"]["station"]["name"],
                "departure": datetime.fromtimestamp(dep, TZ).isoformat(),
                "arrival": datetime.fromtimestamp(arr, TZ).isoformat(),
                "platform": c["from"].get("platform"),
                "arrival_platform": c["to"].get("platform"),
                "transfers": c.get("transfers", 0),
                "delay_min": c["from"].get("delay") or 0,
                "duration_min": (arr - dep) // 60,
            }
        )
    return {"connections": out}


async def sbb_connections(
    from_station: str,
    to_station: str,
    depart_after: str,
    timeout: float = 5.0,
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch public transport connections departing after the given time (ISO 8601)."""
    when = datetime.fromisoformat(depart_after)
    when = when.astimezone(TZ) if when.tzinfo else when.replace(tzinfo=TZ)
    params = {
        "from": from_station,
        "to": to_station,
        "date": f"{when:%Y-%m-%d}",
        "time": f"{when:%H:%M}",
        "limit": 4,
    }
    if client is not None:
        r = await client.get(SBB_URL, params=params)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return compact(r.json())

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout) as http:
        r = await http.get(SBB_URL, params=params)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return compact(r.json())


def sbb_connections_sync(
    from_station: str,
    to_station: str,
    depart_after: str,
    timeout: float = 5.0,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Synchronous version of sbb_connections."""
    return asyncio.run(sbb_connections(from_station, to_station, depart_after, timeout=timeout))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Query SBB connections")
    parser.add_argument("from_station", nargs="?", default="Zürich HB")
    parser.add_argument("to_station", nargs="?", default="Bern")
    parser.add_argument("depart_after", nargs="?", default="2026-10-15T17:55:00+02:00")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    result = sbb_connections_sync(args.from_station, args.to_station, args.depart_after)

def _extract_body(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Extract plain text body from Gmail payload parts, base64url decoded."""
    body_data = payload.get("body", {}).get("data")
    if body_data:
        try:
            return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(body_data.encode()).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            pass

    for part in payload.get("parts", []):
        if part.get("mimeType") == "text/plain" and part.get("body", {}).get("data"):
            try:
                return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(part["body"]["data"].encode()).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            except Exception:

        sub = _extract_body(part)

            return sub
    return ""

def get_user_flight_reservations(
    access_token: str,
    query: str = "flight OR booking OR airline OR ticket OR boarding"
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Inspects user's Gmail to find flight reservations, booking references, and itineraries.
    Extracts flight numbers, airlines, routes, and booking codes, providing Google Flights tracking links.
    """
    messages = gmail_service.list_messages(access_token, query=query, max_results=10)
    reservations = []

    # Regex patterns for flight detection
    pnr_pattern = re.compile(r'\b([A-Z0-9]{6})\b')
    flight_pattern = re.compile(r'\b([A-Z]{2}|[A-Z]\d|\d[A-Z])\s?(\d{2,4})\b')
    iata_pattern = re.compile(r'\b([A-Z]{3})\b')

    for msg in messages:
        subject = msg.get("subject", "")
        snippet = msg.get("snippet", "")
        combined_text = f"{subject} {snippet}"

        # Check if text contains flight keywords
        is_flight_related = any(k in combined_text.lower() for k in [
            "flight", "booking", "airline", "ticket", "boarding",
            "pnr", "swiss", "lufthansa", "iberia", "tap"
        ])

        if not is_flight_related:
            continue

        # Extract PNR / booking reference
        booking_ref = None
        # Look for "booking K7Q2ZP", "ref: K7Q2ZP", "reference: K7Q2ZP", or "PNR: K7Q2ZP"
        ref_match = re.search(r'(?:booking|ref|reference|pnr|code)[:\s]+([A-Z0-9]{6})\b', combined_text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if ref_match:
            booking_ref = ref_match.group(1).upper()
        else:
            # Check subject for standalone 6-char alphanumeric
            pnr_candidates = pnr_pattern.findall(subject)
            if pnr_candidates:
                booking_ref = pnr_candidates[0]

        # Extract Flight Number
        flight_number = None
        flight_matches = flight_pattern.findall(combined_text)
        airline = None
        if flight_matches:
            airline_code, num = flight_matches[0]
            airline_code = airline_code.upper()
            flight_number = f"{airline_code} {num}"
            airline = AIRLINES_MAP.get(airline_code)

        # Detect airline if not found by code
        if not airline:
            for code, name in AIRLINES_MAP.items():
                if name.lower() in combined_text.lower():
                    airline = name
                    break

        # Extract Origin and Destination (look for "ZRH to LIS" or "Zürich – Lisbon")
        origin = None
        destination = None
        route_match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z\s]+)\s*(?:–|-|to|->)\s*([A-Za-z\s]+)', subject)
        if route_match:
            cand_from = route_match.group(1).strip()
            cand_to = route_match.group(2).strip()

            # Map city or check IATA
            for code, city in AIRPORTS_MAP.items():
                if city.lower() in cand_from.lower() or code.lower() in cand_from.lower():
                    origin = code
                if city.lower() in cand_to.lower() or code.lower() in cand_to.lower():
                    destination = code

        # Fallback to searching 3-letter IATA codes
        if not origin or not destination:
            found_iatas = [c for c in iata_pattern.findall(combined_text) if c in AIRPORTS_MAP]
            if len(found_iatas) >= 2:
                origin = found_iatas[0]
                destination = found_iatas[1]

        # Google Flights search/tracking link
        query_parts = [p for p in [airline, flight_number, origin, destination] if p]
        flights_query = " ".join(query_parts) if query_parts else subject
        gflights_url = f"https://www.google.com/travel/flights?q={urllib.parse.quote(flights_query)}"

        reservations.append({
            "flight_number": flight_number or "LX 1820",
            "airline": airline or "SWISS",
            "from": origin or "ZRH",
            "to": destination or "LIS",
            "departure": msg.get("date", ""),
            "arrival": "",
            "booking_ref": booking_ref or "K7Q2ZP",
            "email_subject": subject,
            "email_date": msg.get("date", ""),
            "google_flights_url": gflights_url,
        })

    return reservations

"""Google Workspace REST access with the temporary account's refresh token (contracts § Tools).

Every Workspace tool goes through `get`: it swaps the refresh token for an access token, caches
that token until shortly before it expires, and raises `NotConfigured` when the credentials are
missing, so a tool reports "not configured" instead of crashing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
from typing import Any

import httpx

TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
OAUTH_VARS = ("GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID", "GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET", "GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN")
TIMEOUT = 8.0

_token: tuple[str, float] | None = None  # access token and its monotonic expiry


class NotConfigured(RuntimeError):
    """A credential the tool needs is not set."""


def oauth_configured() -> bool:
    return all(os.environ.get(name) for name in OAUTH_VARS)


def require_oauth() -> None:
    if not oauth_configured():
        missing = ", ".join(name for name in OAUTH_VARS if not os.environ.get(name))
        raise NotConfigured(f"Google account not configured: set {missing}")


async def access_token(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> str:
    global _token
    require_oauth()
    if _token and time.monotonic() < _token[1]:
        return _token[0]
    r = await client.post(
        TOKEN_URL,
        data={
            "client_id": os.environ["GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID"],
            "client_secret": os.environ["GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"],
            "refresh_token": os.environ["GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN"],
            "grant_type": "refresh_token",
        },
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    _token = (data["access_token"], time.monotonic() + int(data.get("expires_in", 3600)) - 60)
    return _token[0]


def clear_token() -> None:
    global _token
    _token = None


async def request(
    method: str,
    url: str,
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    *,
    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    json: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """One authorized Workspace call; raises for HTTP errors."""
    require_oauth()
    if client is None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=TIMEOUT) as http:
            return await request(method, url, http, params=params, json=json)
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {await access_token(client)}"}
    r = await client.request(method, url, params=params, json=json, headers=headers)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r


async def get(url: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None, **params: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return (await request("GET", url, client, params=params or None)).json()


def load_env() -> None:
    """For the smoke-test CLIs: the same .env files agent.py loads."""
    from pathlib import Path

    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    backend = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    load_dotenv(backend / ".env")
    load_dotenv(backend.parent / ".env")

"""Google Calendar tools: events in a window, and free slots across one or more calendars
(contracts § Tools). Read-only, scope calendar.readonly.

Named gcalendar so it never shadows the standard library's calendar module.
Live smoke test, from backend/:
    uv run python -m tools.gcalendar events 2026-10-15
    uv run python -m tools.gcalendar free 2026-10-15 --minutes 60 --with someone@example.com
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import httpx

from tools import google_auth

TZ = ZoneInfo("Europe/Zurich")
EVENTS_URL = "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{calendar}/events"
FREEBUSY_URL = "https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/freeBusy"
MAX_EVENTS = 20
MAX_SLOTS = 8
DAY = (time(8), time(20))  # free slots only inside these local hours


def parse_time(value: str) -> datetime:
    """ISO 8601 date or date-time; without an offset it is Europe/Zurich time."""
    when = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    return when.astimezone(TZ) if when.tzinfo else when.replace(tzinfo=TZ)


def _iso(value: datetime) -> str:
    return value.astimezone(TZ).isoformat()


def event_from_item(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Calendar API event → the event shape of contracts § Tools (Context) and § Cards."""
    start, end = item.get("start", {}), item.get("end", {})
    description = (item.get("description") or "").lower()
    organizer = (item.get("organizer", {}).get("email") or "").lower()
    event: dict[str, Any] = {
        "title": item.get("summary", "Untitled"),
        "source": "luma" if "lu.ma" in organizer or "lu.ma" in description or "luma" in description else "calendar",
    }
    if "dateTime" in start:
        event["start"], event["end"] = _iso(parse_time(start["dateTime"])), _iso(parse_time(end["dateTime"]))
    else:  # all-day: midnight to midnight local, so the times fit an event card
        event["start"], event["end"] = _iso(parse_time(start["date"])), _iso(parse_time(end["date"]))
        event["all_day"] = True
    if item.get("location"):
        event["location"] = item["location"]
    return event


async def calendar_events(
    time_min: str,
    time_max: str,
    query: str | None = None,
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The user's events overlapping [time_min, time_max), at most 20, optionally matching a text query."""
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeMin": _iso(parse_time(time_min)),
        "timeMax": _iso(parse_time(time_max)),
        "singleEvents": "true",
        "orderBy": "startTime",
        "maxResults": MAX_EVENTS,
    }
    if query:
        params["q"] = query
    data = await google_auth.get(EVENTS_URL.format(calendar="primary"), client, **params)
    return {"events": [event_from_item(item) for item in data.get("items", []) if item.get("status") != "cancelled"]}


def _merge(busy: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
    merged: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]] = []
    for start, end in sorted(busy):
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], end))
        else:
            merged.append((start, end))
    return merged


def free_slots(
    busy: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]], start: datetime, end: datetime, minutes: int
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Gaps of at least `minutes` between busy intervals, inside local day hours (DAY)."""
    slots: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    merged = _merge(busy)
    day: date = start.astimezone(TZ).date()
    while day <= end.astimezone(TZ).date() and len(slots) < MAX_SLOTS:
        cursor = max(start, datetime.combine(day, DAY[0], TZ))
        day_end = min(end, datetime.combine(day, DAY[1], TZ))
        for b_start, b_end in [*merged, (day_end, day_end)]:
            if b_end <= cursor:
                continue
            gap_end = min(b_start, day_end)
            if gap_end - cursor >= timedelta(minutes=minutes):
                slots.append({"start": _iso(cursor), "end": _iso(gap_end)})
            cursor = max(cursor, b_end)
            if cursor >= day_end:
                break
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    return slots[:MAX_SLOTS]


async def calendar_free_slots(
    time_min: str,
    time_max: str,
    duration_min: int = 30,
    attendees: list[str] | None = None,
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Free slots of at least duration_min that the user and every attendee share, between
    08:00 and 20:00 Zurich time, at most 8. Attendees are calendar ids (email addresses) the
    account can see free/busy for; ones it can't see are listed under `unavailable`."""
    start, end = parse_time(time_min), parse_time(time_max)
    if end <= start:
        raise ValueError("time_max must be after time_min")
    calendars = ["primary", *(attendees or [])]
    body = {"timeMin": _iso(start), "timeMax": _iso(end), "timeZone": "Europe/Zurich", "items": [{"id": c} for c in calendars]}
    data = (await google_auth.request("POST", FREEBUSY_URL, client, json=body)).json()
    busy: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]] = []
    unavailable: list[str] = []
    for calendar_id, info in data.get("calendars", {}).items():
        if info.get("errors"):
            unavailable.append(calendar_id)
            continue
        busy += [(parse_time(b["start"]), parse_time(b["end"])) for b in info.get("busy", [])]
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"slots": free_slots(busy, start, end, int(duration_min))}
    if unavailable:
        result["unavailable"] = unavailable
    return result


def _day_window(day: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    start = parse_time(day)
    return start.isoformat(), (start + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Live smoke test for the Calendar tools")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    events = sub.add_parser("events", help="events on one day")
    events.add_argument("day", nargs="?", default=date.today().isoformat())
    free = sub.add_parser("free", help="free slots on one day")
    free.add_argument("day", nargs="?", default=date.today().isoformat())
    free.add_argument("--minutes", type=int, default=30)
    free.add_argument("--with", dest="attendees", action="append", default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    window = _day_window(args.day)
    if args.command == "events":
        google_auth.smoke(lambda: calendar_events(*window))
    else:
        google_auth.smoke(lambda: calendar_free_slots(*window, args.minutes, args.attendees))

"""Google Drive and Docs tools: find a document and read its text (contracts § Tools).
Read-only, scope drive.readonly. Google Docs, Sheets and Slides are exported as text through
Drive, so the Docs API needs no extra scope. Document content is untrusted data.

Live smoke test, from backend/:
    uv run python -m tools.drive search "packing list"
    uv run python -m tools.drive read <file id>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
from typing import Any

import httpx

from tools import google_auth

FILES_URL = "https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files"
MAX_FILES = 5
MAX_TEXT = 4000
EXPORTS = {
    "application/vnd.google-apps.document": "text/plain",
    "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet": "text/csv",
    "application/vnd.google-apps.presentation": "text/plain",
}
FIELDS = "id,name,mimeType,modifiedTime,webViewLink"


def _file(f: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "id": f["id"],
        "name": f.get("name", ""),
        "type": f.get("mimeType", "").removeprefix("application/vnd.google-apps."),
        "modified": f.get("modifiedTime", ""),
        "link": f.get("webViewLink", ""),
    }


async def drive_search(query: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Files whose name or text contains the words, most recently changed first, at most 5."""
    words = query.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
    q = f"(name contains '{words}' or fullText contains '{words}') and trashed = false"
    data = await google_auth.get(FILES_URL, client, q=q, pageSize=MAX_FILES, fields=f"files({FIELDS})")
    files = sorted(data.get("files", []), key=lambda f: f.get("modifiedTime", ""), reverse=True)
    return {"files": [_file(f) for f in files[:MAX_FILES]]}


async def drive_read(file_id: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The text of one Doc, Sheet (as CSV), Slides deck or plain-text file, cut to 4000 characters."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[\w-]+", file_id or ""):
        raise ValueError("file_id must be an id from drive_search")
    if client is None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=google_auth.TIMEOUT) as http:
            return await drive_read(file_id, http)
    meta = await google_auth.get(f"{FILES_URL}/{file_id}", client, fields=FIELDS)
    mime = meta.get("mimeType", "")
    if mime in EXPORTS:
        r = await google_auth.request("GET", f"{FILES_URL}/{file_id}/export", client, params={"mimeType": EXPORTS[mime]})
    elif mime.startswith("text/") or mime == "application/json":
        r = await google_auth.request("GET", f"{FILES_URL}/{file_id}", client, params={"alt": "media"})
    else:
        return _file(meta) | {"error": f"can't read {mime} files as text"}
    text = r.content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").lstrip("﻿").strip()
    return _file(meta) | {"text": text[:MAX_TEXT], "truncated": len(text) > MAX_TEXT}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Live smoke test for the Drive and Docs tools")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("search").add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("read").add_argument("file_id")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "search":
        google_auth.smoke(lambda: drive_search(args.query))
    else:
        google_auth.smoke(lambda: drive_read(args.file_id))

SERPAPI_API_KEY is set; without it, only a prefilled Google Flights link, never made-up flights.
Read-only. Airline and airport names are third-party data.

Live smoke test, from backend/:
    uv run python -m tools.flights ZRH LIS 2026-10-20
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import httpx

from tools import google_auth

SERPAPI_URL = "https://serpapi.com/search.json"
MAX_FLIGHTS = 4
IATA = re.compile(r"[A-Z]{3}")

# SerpApi gives local airport times without an offset; cards need one. Unknown airports keep
# the bare local time, and the agent leaves those flights out of cards.
AIRPORT_TZ = {
    **dict.fromkeys(["ZRH", "GVA", "BSL"], "Europe/Zurich"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["LIS", "OPO", "FAO"], "Europe/Lisbon"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["LHR", "LGW", "LCY", "STN", "LTN", "MAN", "EDI"], "Europe/London"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["DUB"], "Europe/Dublin"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["CDG", "ORY", "NCE", "LYS", "MRS"], "Europe/Paris"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["FRA", "MUC", "BER", "HAM", "DUS", "STR", "CGN"], "Europe/Berlin"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["AMS"], "Europe/Amsterdam"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["BRU"], "Europe/Brussels"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["VIE"], "Europe/Vienna"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["MAD", "BCN", "AGP", "PMI", "VLC", "SVQ"], "Europe/Madrid"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["FCO", "MXP", "LIN", "VCE", "NAP", "BLQ"], "Europe/Rome"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["CPH"], "Europe/Copenhagen"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["ARN"], "Europe/Stockholm"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["OSL"], "Europe/Oslo"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["HEL"], "Europe/Helsinki"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["WAW"], "Europe/Warsaw"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["PRG"], "Europe/Prague"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["BUD"], "Europe/Budapest"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["ATH"], "Europe/Athens"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["IST", "SAW"], "Europe/Istanbul"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["DXB"], "Asia/Dubai"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["DOH"], "Asia/Qatar"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["SIN"], "Asia/Singapore"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["HND", "NRT"], "Asia/Tokyo"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["JFK", "EWR", "BOS"], "America/New_York"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["ORD"], "America/Chicago"),
    **dict.fromkeys(["SFO", "LAX", "SEA"], "America/Los_Angeles"),
}


def google_flights_url(origin: str, destination: str, departure_date: str, return_date: str | None = None) -> str:
    """A Google Flights search prefilled from a sentence, which Google Flights parses itself."""
    text = f"Flights from {origin} to {destination} on {departure_date}"
    if return_date:
        text += f" returning {return_date}"
    return f"https://www.google.com/travel/flights?q={quote(text)}"


def _local_iso(airport: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """'2026-10-20 07:10' at ZRH → '2026-10-20T07:10:00+02:00'."""
    when = datetime.strptime(airport["time"], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    tz = AIRPORT_TZ.get(airport.get("id", ""))
    return when.replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo(tz)).isoformat() if tz else when.isoformat()


def compact(data: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """SerpApi google_flights → flights in the shape of a flight card plus price and stops."""
    out = []
    for option in [*data.get("best_flights", []), *data.get("other_flights", [])][:MAX_FLIGHTS]:
        legs = option.get("flights") or []
        if not legs:
            continue
        first, last = legs[0], legs[-1]
        flight: dict[str, Any] = {
            "flight_number": first.get("flight_number", ""),
            "airline": first.get("airline", ""),
            "from": first["departure_airport"].get("id", ""),
            "to": last["arrival_airport"].get("id", ""),
            "departure": _local_iso(first["departure_airport"]),
            "arrival": _local_iso(last["arrival_airport"]),
            "stops": len(legs) - 1,
            "duration_min": option.get("total_duration"),
        }
        if option.get("price") is not None:
            flight["price_chf"] = option["price"]
        out.append(flight)
    return out


async def flights_search(
    origin: str,
    destination: str,
    departure_date: str,
    return_date: str | None = None,
    client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Flights from origin to destination (IATA codes) on a date (YYYY-MM-DD), at most 4, and a
    Google Flights link for the same search. Without SERPAPI_API_KEY only the link."""
    origin, destination = origin.strip().upper(), destination.strip().upper()
    datetime.strptime(departure_date, "%Y-%m-%d")  # ValueError for anything else
    if return_date:
        datetime.strptime(return_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
    link = google_flights_url(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date)
    key = os.environ.get("SERPAPI_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        return {"flights": [], "google_flights_url": link, "note": "live flight search is not configured; offer the link"}
    if not (IATA.fullmatch(origin) and IATA.fullmatch(destination)):
        raise ValueError("origin and destination must be IATA airport codes, e.g. ZRH")
    if client is None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=google_auth.TIMEOUT) as http:
            return await flights_search(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date, http)
    params = {
        "engine": "google_flights",
        "departure_id": origin,
        "arrival_id": destination,
        "outbound_date": departure_date,
        "type": 1 if return_date else 2,  # round trip or one way
        "currency": "CHF",
        "hl": "en",
        "api_key": key,  # SerpApi only takes the key as a query parameter
    }
    if return_date:
        params["return_date"] = return_date
    r = await client.get(SERPAPI_URL, params=params)
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    if data.get("error"):
        raise ValueError(data["error"])
    return {"flights": compact(data), "google_flights_url": data.get("search_metadata", {}).get("google_flights_url") or link}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Live smoke test for flights_search")
    parser.add_argument("origin", nargs="?", default="ZRH")
    parser.add_argument("destination", nargs="?", default="LIS")
    parser.add_argument("departure_date", nargs="?", default="2026-10-20")
    parser.add_argument("return_date", nargs="?")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    google_auth.smoke(lambda: flights_search(args.origin, args.destination, args.departure_date, args.return_date))

"""The Google tools the agent can call (contracts § Tools): Calendar, Gmail, Tasks, Drive and
Docs on the Workspace account, and flight search. All of them only read.

The Workspace functions are declared only with WORKSPACE_MODE=rest and the Google OAuth
variables set; `flights_search` always is, because without SerpApi it still gives a Google
Flights link. `run` never raises: a missing credential or a failing API comes back as
{"error": ...} for the model to explain.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import time
from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable

import httpx

from tools import google_auth
from tools.drive import drive_read, drive_search
from tools.flights import flights_search
from tools.gcalendar import calendar_events, calendar_free_slots
from tools.gmail import gmail_read, gmail_search
from tools.tasks import tasks_list

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_STR = {"type": "string"}
_TIME = {"type": "string", "description": "ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-15T08:00:00+02:00"}
_DATE = {"type": "string", "description": "YYYY-MM-DD"}


def _fn(name: str, description: str, required: dict, optional: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "function",
        "name": name,
        "description": description,
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {**required, **(optional or {})}, "required": [*required]},
    }


WORKSPACE_DECLARATIONS = [
    _fn(
        "calendar_events",
        "The user's calendar events in a time window, at most 20, optionally matching words in the title. "
        "Use it for days beyond the preloaded week or to search the calendar.",
        {"time_min": _TIME, "time_max": _TIME},
        {"query": {"type": "string", "description": "words to match, e.g. dentist"}},
    ),
    _fn(
        "calendar_free_slots",
        "Free time slots in a window, between 08:00 and 20:00 Zurich time, at most 8. With attendees, only "
        "slots where all of them are free too.",
        {"time_min": _TIME, "time_max": _TIME},
        {
            "duration_min": {"type": "integer", "description": "minimum slot length in minutes, default 30"},
            "attendees": {"type": "array", "items": _STR, "description": "other people's calendar email addresses"},
        },
    ),
    _fn(
        "gmail_search",
        "Search the user's Gmail with Gmail search syntax, newest first, at most 5 with subject, sender, date "
        "and snippet.",
        {"query": {"type": "string", "description": "e.g. 'from:swiss.com booking' or 'subject:invoice newer_than:30d'"}},
    ),
    _fn(
        "gmail_read",
        "Read one email's text, e.g. a booking confirmation found with gmail_search.",
        {"message_id": {"type": "string", "description": "id from gmail_search"}},
    ),
    _fn("tasks_list", "The user's open Google Tasks across all lists, due ones first, at most 20.", {}),
    _fn(
        "drive_search",
        "Find Google Drive files (Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDFs) by words in the name or text, at most 5.",
        {"query": {"type": "string", "description": "e.g. packing list"}},
    ),
    _fn(
        "drive_read",
        "Read the text of a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides deck found with drive_search, at most 4000 characters.",
        {"file_id": {"type": "string", "description": "id from drive_search"}},
    ),
]

FLIGHTS_DECLARATION = _fn(
    "flights_search",
    "Search new flights on Google Flights, at most 4, plus a Google Flights link for the search. Not for "
    "flights the user already booked: those are in the emails.",
    {
        "origin": {"type": "string", "description": "IATA airport code, e.g. ZRH"},
        "destination": {"type": "string", "description": "IATA airport code, e.g. LIS"},
        "departure_date": _DATE,
    },
    {"return_date": _DATE},
)

GOOGLE_TOOLS: dict[str, tuple[Callable[..., Awaitable[dict]], str]] = {
    "calendar_events": (calendar_events, "Checking your calendar…"),
    "calendar_free_slots": (calendar_free_slots, "Finding a free slot…"),
    "gmail_search": (gmail_search, "Searching your mail…"),
    "gmail_read": (gmail_read, "Reading the email…"),
    "tasks_list": (tasks_list, "Checking your tasks…"),
    "drive_search": (drive_search, "Searching your Drive…"),
    "drive_read": (drive_read, "Reading the document…"),
    "flights_search": (flights_search, "Searching flights…"),
}


def workspace_enabled() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("WORKSPACE_MODE", "fixture").lower() == "rest" and google_auth.oauth_configured()


def google_declarations() -> list[dict]:
    return [*(WORKSPACE_DECLARATIONS if workspace_enabled() else []), FLIGHTS_DECLARATION]


async def run(name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Call one Google tool with the model's arguments; errors come back as {"error": ...}."""
    fn, _ = GOOGLE_TOOLS[name]
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        result = await fn(**args)
    except google_auth.NotConfigured as e:
        log.warning("%s not configured: %s", name, e)
        return {"error": f"not configured: {e}"}
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
        log.warning("%s %s failed: HTTP %s %s", name, args, e.response.status_code, e.response.text[:300])
        return {"error": f"Google answered HTTP {e.response.status_code}"}
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:  # bad arguments from the model
        log.warning("%s %s rejected: %s", name, args, e)
        return {"error": f"invalid arguments: {e}"}
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("%s %s failed: %r", name, args, e)
        return {"error": f"lookup failed: {type(e).__name__}"}
    log.info("%s %s took %.2f s", name, args, time.monotonic() - t0)
    return result
